scenarios.title: Evidence and conflicting records
scenarios.summary: Two synthetic records seem to disagree about one item. The lead answers under the household stock guard (usually 'could not confirm'); a separate record review quotes both records, says the discrepancy is unresolved, and lists the evidence that would settle it.
scenarios.prompt: The pantry stock says we have 3 tins of tomatoes but the shopping list says we bought 12 this month. Which is right?

evaluations.title: Six Eyes on the -11 team evaluation, cluster-aware
evaluations.headline: 8 distinct tasks: no verdict meets the 20-task floor; specialist consultation shows no established quality gain and about 1.4 s extra latency

evaluations.title: Allocation decision evaluation, held-out v1 (anomaly, 8 cases)
evaluations.headline: as frozen: production 5/8, candidate 7/8; the candidate was not promoted

records.role: shopping-list line, an unticked item under 'Need'

evidence_review.why: the two records are not measuring the same thing: the pantry line is a count as of 2026-10-01; the list line is an unticked 'Need' entry with no purchase date. Neither establishes the number of tins in the house today, and neither contradicts the other outright.
needed: a dated purchase record (receipt or order) for the tinned tomatoes, to say whether 12 were actually bought and when
a physical count of the tins now, to compare with the 2026-10-01 stock line
